title: Gemini interactive source inventory
adaptation: EncapsulatorP Atlas

records.boundary: This is a finite search for even totals from 20 through 200. Finding every pair in this range does not prove Goldbach’s conjecture.
adaptation: Enumerate all valid radii independently of animation frames.
Label 1 correctly as non-prime.
Fit the full number line to the viewport; add discrete step control.

records.boundary: The reset and counter are defined animation rules in arbitrary units. This is not a physical model, demonstrated monodromy or construction of Riemann sheets. “Bitemporal” preserves the supplied concept’s name.
adaptation: Preserve the original ordered finite-step recurrence, reset assignment and dt*0.05 rotating reference mesh.
Retain four bounded, thick, color-distinguished pass trails at their true coordinates; offer current-pass and original-view comparison.
Mark both reset endpoints and a dashed prescribed jump; Catch next reset pauses at the next unchanged event.
Retain full controls and trajectory in a projected Canvas fallback when WebGL is unavailable.
Use explicit arbitrary units and finite reset rules; replace hole-center claim with inner-rim crossing.
Quiet the wireframe in overlay modes, strengthen trail width/contrast and fit narrow-stage camera framing while preserving relative zoom.

records.boundary: A finite parameter grid and transient cutoff can hide narrow windows or slow approach. Preset names orient the reader; the HUD gives sample counts rather than a hard-coded stability verdict.
adaptation: Remove hard-coded stability classifications.
Label recorded orbit by its actual iterations51–150.
Keep source sampling choices explicit; preserve bifurcation and orbit panels.

records.boundary: This is a toy inspired by Collatz-style branching. No physical relation to early dark energy or derived Poincaré return map is established. Staying within the sampled range is not a proof of boundedness.
adaptation: Replace unsupported cosmological labels with recurrence parameters.
Remove value cap from iteration; stop after raw first escape above100.
Replace bounded/unstable verdict with finite run status.
Subscribe calculations only to actual parameter changes.
Restore the original named Poincaré exhibit as a dedicated route with all five source parameter ranges and exact capped replay available for comparison.

additionalViews.description: Explicitly named Poincaré return-map specimen with leg-by-leg cobweb playback, orbit focus, original 0–20 view and separately labeled original capped replay.

records.boundary: These coordinate pictures reveal the selected sample. They do not establish manifold topology, a growth rate, or a global geometric property of the infinite sequence.
adaptation: Rename Topology control to Coordinates.
Start normalized triples at n3, excluding division by zero.
Remove unsupported roughly2n growth assumption; scale from finite ratios.
Use instanced meshes for the original addition/subtraction point clouds.

records.boundary: Reset and retention come from the programmed update rules. A circle does not itself force information loss, and this drawn helix is not a constructed Riemann surface.
adaptation: Give both modes the same accumulation rate μ per unit time.
Describe reset/retention as chosen rules, not consequences of topology.
Rename Riemann Helix to lifted helix in the exhibit.
Preserve paused trail, clear reset particles, and follow height with camera.

records.reason: The source remains recorded as a coordinate-only alternative. The dedicated original Recamán obstruction explorer is now selected separately and restores its own exact red-hole and Möbius mappings.

records.boundary: Exact prime-indicator projection energies for a selected even total N from 10 through 150. The finite ratio does not prove Goldbach’s conjecture.
adaptation: Preserve all source controls, mirror connectors and exact E+, E− and rho definitions with no new normalization.
Expose folded-orbit energy contributions, central fixed-point multiplicity and the finite prime-pair list.
Use non-prime instead of composite for a category that includes 1.

records.reason: The High fit label is based on a count heuristic, not a goodness-of-fit test; resets alter the dynamics and the default can generate no bursts.

records.boundary: Finite principal-branch tolerance and escape classification, with a separate stochastic logarithm-sheet experiment. No finite sample certifies convergence or Shell–Thron membership.
adaptation: Preserve the original complex seed, four parameter ranges, real critical-base presets, basin palette and white/blue/red orbit layers.
Preserve one Gaussian perturbation per base and independent k in {−1,0,+1} at each update, not a cumulative sheet walk.
Use finite labels and one-based escape steps; keep the original tolerance and numerical escape limits.
Handle zero and the original near-zero numerical cutoff explicitly; exclude undefined perturbations from the survival denominator.
Add keyboard and numeric base selection; retain samples across resize and progressively rasterize the basin under the shared visibility lifecycle.

records.boundary: Red holes are finite unvisited scalar values placed with the source’s chosen mapping. The display does not prove a manifold or topological obstruction.
adaptation: Restore exact source delay and twisted Möbius mappings, addition/subtraction colors and in-scene red-hole loci with the original sampling stride.
Retain source camera, N range, holes toggle, theme, rotation and orbit controls; add keyboard access.
Use N terms including a0 and N−1 transitions for the backward ratio.
Provide WebGL and projected Canvas rendering of the same coordinates and camera, with full finite statistics in either view.
Fit the complete original cloud on narrow stages by responsive camera distance; preserve relative user zoom and reset framing.

records.boundary: Layer names are illustrative labels, not a physical renormalization; information lost is a heuristic readout. The Hopf panel is the exact normal form r' = mu r - r^3 with stable cycle radius sqrt(mu).
adaptation: Port tab 1 of the c3.2z workspace (drawRG, dimensionState, renderDimension, paintDimension) with its constants, unit tree, ranges and defaults unchanged.
Bring the knot r/e and third-layer controls that drive the lattice into the same exhibit.
White instrument stage and the Atlas ramp (lavender, periwinkle, sapphire, amber) in place of slate, sky, mint and gold.
Add Next layer, Play/Pause and a live R^2 = max(0, mu) check; pause when hidden or under reduced motion.
State that layer names and the information-loss figure are illustrative, and that digits of c are a symbolic alphabet.

runtime.description: Local Atlas adapter preserving the selected supplied topic logic and visual concepts. Remote WH scaffolds and message bridge excluded.
runtime.requestPolicy: No runtime network calls; exhibit CSP connect-src none.
runtime.originalSourcePolicy: Only original topic scripts are published as text; the remote scaffold is retained in the supplied uploads, not executed here.
